ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Initially, a switch $S$ is unshorted in the circuit shown in the figure on the right, a capacitor of capacitance $2 C$ carries the electric charge $q_{0}$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is uncharged, and there are no electric currents in both coils of inductance $L$ and $2 L$, respectively. The capacitor starts to discharge and at the moment when the current in the coils reaches its maximum value, the switch $S$ is instantly shorted. Find the maximum current $I_{\max }$ through the switch $S$ thereafter.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangular outer loop. The upper part of the left branch is a capacitor 2C, with the upper plate marked as + and the lower plate marked as - beside it; the lower part of the left branch is a capacitor C. The upper part of the right branch is an inductor L, and the lower part is an inductor 2L. The switch S connects the left and right midpoints, and in the figure the switch is initially open. Reasoning: Reading from the figure, when S is open, the outside forms a series loop: the two capacitors 2C, C on the left side are in series with the two inductors L, 2L on the right side. Let the charge variable of the upper 2C capacitor be Q1, and the charge variable of the lower C capacitor be Q2; their voltages are respectively Q1/(2C), Q2/C. Since the midpoint between the two capacitors on the left side is isolated when S is open, the charge constraint Q1 - Q2 = q0 is maintained. When the current reaches its maximum, the capacitor electric energy is minimized under this constraint: U = Q1^2/(4C) + Q2^2/(2C). Let Q2 = Q1 - q0; minimizing gives Q1 = 2q0/3, Q2 = -q0/3. The initial electric energy is q0^2/(4C), and at this time the capacitor electric energy is q0^2/(6C), so the lost electric energy is q0^2/(12C). This part becomes the magnetic energy of the two series inductors: (1/2)(L+2L) I0^2 = (3L/2)I0^2, so I0 = q0/(3sqrt(2LC)). After S is closed instantaneously, the upper half in the figure becomes an LC oscillator composed of 2C and L, and the lower half becomes an LC oscillator composed of C and 2L. Their angular frequencies are the same: omega = 1/sqrt(2LC). At the instant of closing, the capacitor voltages are continuous, v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C), v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C), and the currents of the two inductors are both I0. Taking the corresponding directions to write the inductor currents: i1(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v1/(L omega)] sin(omega t), i2(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v2/(2L omega)] sin(omega t). Substituting gives i1(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) + [2q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t), i2(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) - [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t). The current through the switch is the magnitude of the difference between the currents of the inductors on the two sides: I_S = |i1 - i2| = |q0/sqrt(2LC) · sin(omega t)|, therefore its maximum value is q0/sqrt(2LC).

method.method_draft: From the diagram, read the open-switch circuit as one outer series loop: capacitors 2C and C on the left, inductors L and 2L on the right, and the switch S connecting their midpoints. Let Q1 be the charge on the upper 2C capacitor and Q2 the charge on the lower C capacitor, with voltages Q1/(2C) and Q2/C. While S is open, the midpoint between the capacitors is isolated, so Q1 - Q2 = q0. At the instant of maximum series current, the electric energy of the two capacitors is minimized under this constraint, equivalently U = Q1^2/(4C) + Q2^2/(2C) is minimized subject to Q1 - Q2 = q0, giving Q1 = 2q0/3 and Q2 = -q0/3. Use energy conservation before switching to get the common inductor current just before closure: the lost capacitor energy equals (1/2)(L+2L)I0^2, so I0 = q0/(3sqrt(2LC)). After S is shorted, the image topology splits into two LC oscillators sharing the midpoint: upper oscillator L with 2C, lower oscillator 2L with C. Both have angular frequency omega = 1/sqrt(2LC). Use initial voltages v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C), v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C), and initial inductor currents both equal to I0 to write i1(t) for the upper inductor and i2(t) for the lower inductor. The switch current is the difference |i1 - i2|; the cosine parts cancel and the sine term has amplitude q0/sqrt(2LC).

推理：按图读出，S 断开时外侧构成一个串联回路：左侧两个电容 2C、C 与右侧两个电感 L、2L 串联。设上方 2C 电容的电荷变量为 Q1，下方 C 电容的电荷变量为 Q2，其电压分别为 Q1/(2C)、Q2/C。由于左侧两电容之间的中点在 S 断开时孤立，保持电荷约束 Q1 - Q2 = q0。电流达到最大时，电容电能在该约束下最小：U = Q1^2/(4C) + Q2^2/(2C)。令 Q2 = Q1 - q0，极小化得 Q1 = 2q0/3，Q2 = -q0/3。初始电能为 q0^2/(4C)，此时电容电能为 q0^2/(6C)，损失的电能为 q0^2/(12C)。这部分变为两个串联电感的磁能：(1/2)(L+2L) I0^2 = (3L/2)I0^2，所以 I0 = q0/(3sqrt(2LC))。
S 瞬间闭合后，图中上半部分成为由 2C 与 L 构成的 LC 振荡器，下半部分成为由 C 与 2L 构成的 LC 振荡器。两者角频率相同：omega = 1/sqrt(2LC)。闭合瞬间电容电压连续，v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C)，v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C)，两个电感电流均为 I0。取相应方向写电感电流：i1(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v1/(L omega)] sin(omega t)，i2(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v2/(2L omega)] sin(omega t)。代入得 i1(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) + [2q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t)，i2(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) - [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t)。通过开关的电流为两侧电感电流之差的大小：I_S = |i1 - i2| = |q0/sqrt(2LC) · sin(omega t)|，因此其最大值为 q0/sqrt(2LC)。

method.method_draft: From the diagram, identify that with S open the two capacitors and two inductors form a single series outer loop, while closing S joins the capacitor midpoint to the inductor midpoint. Before closing, use only charge conservation and the maximum-current condition. Let Q1 be the charge on 2C and Q2 on C. Since the capacitor midpoint is isolated while S is open, Q1 - Q2 = q0. At maximum current, dI/dt = 0 in the series loop, so the net capacitor voltage around the loop must vanish: Q1/(2C) + Q2/C = 0. Solve these two equations to get Q1 = 2q0/3 and Q2 = -q0/3, so immediately after closure v1 = q0/(3C) across the upper LC pair and v2 = -q0/(3C) across the lower LC pair. Define the switch current, up to sign, as j = i_L - i_2L, the difference between the currents in the upper and lower inductors at the midpoint. At the switching instant, the former series current makes i_L(0) = i_2L(0), so j(0) = 0. After closure, the upper pair L,2C and lower pair 2L,C have the same frequency omega = 1/sqrt(2LC), so j obeys j'' + omega^2 j = 0. Its initial derivative is j'(0) = v1/L - v2/(2L) = q0/(2LC). Therefore the oscillation amplitude is j_max = j'(0)/omega = q0/sqrt(2LC), which is the maximum current through S.

图像描述：图中左侧支路有两个串联电容，上方电容标为 2C，并标出初始上板为正、下板为负；下方电容标为 C。右侧支路有两个串联线圈，上方电感为 L，下方电感为 2L。上下导线把左右两支路连成外回路，中间有开关 S 连接左侧两个电容的中点和右侧两个电感的中点；图中 S 初始断开。

推理：S 断开时，两个电容和两个电感构成一个外部串联回路。设此时上方 2C 电容的电荷为 Q1，下方 C 电容的电荷为 Q2。由于 S 断开时左侧电容中点是孤立节点，其电荷守恒，所以有 Q1 - Q2 = q0。题设在两线圈电流达到最大时闭合 S，此时串联回路电流最大，因此 dI/dt = 0，回路中电容电压代数和为零：Q1/(2C) + Q2/C = 0。联立两式得 Q1 = 2q0/3，Q2 = -q0/3。

因此闭合瞬间，上半部分 LC 支路的电压为 v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C)，下半部分 LC 支路的电压为 v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C)。闭合后，上支路由 L 与 2C 组成，下支路由 2L 与 C 组成，两者固有角频率相同，均为 omega = 1/sqrt(2LC)。令通过开关的电流大小对应于两电感电流之差 j = i_L - i_2L。闭合瞬间原先为同一串联电流，所以 i_L(0) = i_2L(0)，故 j(0) = 0。其初始变化率为 j'(0) = v1/L - v2/(2L) = q0/(3CL) + q0/(6CL) = q0/(2LC)。于是 j 作简谐振动，满足 j'' + omega^2 j = 0，其最大值为 j_max = j'(0)/omega = [q0/(2LC)] sqrt(2LC) = q0/sqrt(2LC)。这就是之后通过开关 S 的最大电流。

method.CoT_final:
图像描述：图中左侧支路有两个串联电容，上方电容标为 2C，并标出初始上板为正、下板为负；下方电容标为 C。右侧支路有两个串联线圈，上方电感为 L，下方电感为 2L。上下导线把左右两支路连成外回路，中间有开关 S 连接左侧两个电容的中点和右侧两个电感的中点；图中 S 初始断开。

推理：S 断开时，两个电容和两个电感构成一个外部串联回路。设此时上方 2C 电容的电荷为 Q1，下方 C 电容的电荷为 Q2。由于 S 断开时左侧电容中点是孤立节点，其电荷守恒，所以有 Q1 - Q2 = q0。题设在两线圈电流达到最大时闭合 S，此时串联回路电流最大，因此 dI/dt = 0，回路中电容电压代数和为零：Q1/(2C) + Q2/C = 0。联立两式得 Q1 = 2q0/3，Q2 = -q0/3。

因此闭合瞬间，上半部分 LC 支路的电压为 v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C)，下半部分 LC 支路的电压为 v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C)。闭合后，上支路由 L 与 2C 组成，下支路由 2L 与 C 组成，两者固有角频率相同，均为 omega = 1/sqrt(2LC)。令通过开关的电流大小对应于两电感电流之差 j = i_L - i_2L。闭合瞬间原先为同一串联电流，所以 i_L(0) = i_2L(0)，故 j(0) = 0。其初始变化率为 j'(0) = v1/L - v2/(2L) = q0/(3CL) + q0/(6CL) = q0/(2LC)。于是 j 作简谐振动，满足 j'' + omega^2 j = 0，其最大值为 j_max = j'(0)/omega = [q0/(2LC)] sqrt(2LC) = q0/sqrt(2LC)。这就是之后通过开关 S 的最大电流。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route avoids computing the pre-switch current or writing full individual oscillator solutions; it derives a direct harmonic equation for the switch-current difference and obtains its amplitude from the initial derivative.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image is needed to see that S bridges the two midpoints, so after closure the switch current equals the mismatch between the upper and lower inductor currents; it also identifies the paired values L with 2C and 2L with C.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text provides the initial charge state and the timing of the shorting operation at maximum coil current, which justifies the zero net capacitor voltage condition before closure and equal inductor currents at closure.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use isolated-node charge conservation, KVL/dI/dt = 0 at maximum current in an LC loop, inductor law di/dt = v/L, and the fact that both post-switch LC pairs have the same natural frequency.

raw_record.original_question: Initially, a switch $S$ is unshorted in the circuit shown in the figure, a capacitor of capacitance $2C$ carries the electric charge $q_{0}$, a capacitor of capacitance $C$ is uncharged, and there are no electric currents in both coils of inductance $L$ and $2L$, respectively. The capacitor starts to discharge and at the moment when the current in the coils reaches its maximum value, the switch $S$ is instantly shorted. Find the maximum current $I_{\max}$ through the switch $S$ thereafter.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows a rectangular outer loop. The upper part of the left branch is a capacitor 2C, with the upper plate marked as + and the lower plate marked as - beside it; the lower part of the left branch is a capacitor C. The upper part of the right branch is an inductor L, and the lower part is an inductor 2L. The switch S connects the left and right midpoints, and in the figure the switch is initially open.
Reasoning: Reading from the figure, when S is open, the outside forms a series loop: the two capacitors 2C, C on the left side are in series with the two inductors L, 2L on the right side. Let the charge variable of the upper 2C capacitor be Q1, and the charge variable of the lower C capacitor be Q2; their voltages are respectively Q1/(2C), Q2/C. Since the midpoint between the two capacitors on the left side is isolated when S is open, the charge constraint Q1 - Q2 = q0 is maintained. When the current reaches its maximum, the capacitor electric energy is minimized under this constraint: U = Q1^2/(4C) + Q2^2/(2C). Let Q2 = Q1 - q0; minimizing gives Q1 = 2q0/3, Q2 = -q0/3. The initial electric energy is q0^2/(4C), and at this time the capacitor electric energy is q0^2/(6C), so the lost electric energy is q0^2/(12C). This part becomes the magnetic energy of the two series inductors: (1/2)(L+2L) I0^2 = (3L/2)I0^2, so I0 = q0/(3sqrt(2LC)).
After S is closed instantaneously, the upper half in the figure becomes an LC oscillator composed of 2C and L, and the lower half becomes an LC oscillator composed of C and 2L. Their angular frequencies are the same: omega = 1/sqrt(2LC). At the instant of closing, the capacitor voltages are continuous, v1 = Q1/(2C) = q0/(3C), v2 = Q2/C = -q0/(3C), and the currents of the two inductors are both I0. Taking the corresponding directions to write the inductor currents: i1(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v1/(L omega)] sin(omega t), i2(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v2/(2L omega)] sin(omega t). Substituting gives i1(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) + [2q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t), i2(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) - [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t). The current through the switch is the magnitude of the difference between the currents of the inductors on the two sides: I_S = |i1 - i2| = |q0/sqrt(2LC) · sin(omega t)|, therefore its maximum value is q0/sqrt(2LC).

claims.claim: Taking the corresponding direction, write the upper branch inductor current i1(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v1/(L omega)] sin(omega t).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Taking the corresponding direction, write the inductor current: i1(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v1/(L omega)] sin(omega t)

claims.claim: Taking the corresponding direction, write the lower-branch inductor current as i2(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v2/(2L omega)] sin(omega t).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: i2(t) = I0 cos(omega t) + [v2/(2L omega)] sin(omega t)

claims.claim: Substituting gives i1(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) + [2q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Substituting gives i1(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) + [2q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t)

claims.claim: Substituting gives i2(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) - [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: i2(t) = [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]cos(omega t) - [q0/(3sqrt(2LC))]sin(omega t)

claims.claim: The current through the switch is I_S = |i1 - i2| = |q0/sqrt(2LC) · sin(omega t)|.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The current through the switch is the magnitude of the difference between the inductor currents on the two sides: I_S = |i1 - i2| = |q0/sqrt(2LC) · sin(omega t)|

claims.claim: The maximum current through the switch is q0/sqrt(2LC).
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore its maximum value is q0/sqrt(2LC).
